title: `canvas push` command
description: commands/push.py: checks (unmerged paths, conflict markers, clean tree unless --allow-dirty, canvas/main ancestor of HEAD, validate, live staleness check of touched objects), plan display and confirmation (--yes, --dry-run, --confirm-grading-change, --no-delete), backup, apply in write mode, refetch, id write-back commit, partial-failure message.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md 'Push rules', 'Example session'; CONTRACTS.md sections 9, 10, 11.
Owns: commands/push.py, tests/test_push.py (end-to-end over FakeCanvas in tmp repos).
High risk.
After apply: refetch and call snapshot(..., extra_parent=HEAD) with the Bodies recorded during apply, then gitops.fast_forward(). If the snapshot differs from HEAD in anything but ids and .canvas/, stop and report (don't fast-forward). No separate write-back commit (SPEC 'Push rules' steps 4-5). Flags include --confirm-notify.
acceptance_criteria: Each refusal case has a test with the documented message; second push after success is a no-op; partial failure leaves a state that pull+push completes; a concurrent remote edit between fetch and push is refused as StaleRemote; tests pass. After a push that creates objects, the user's branch fast-forwards to a canvas/main containing the new ids and `canvas status` is clean.

title: Differ and writers: assignments and groups

Overrides are a separate bead.

High risk. All deletes and risky updates go through ApplyContext.guard.
acceptance_criteria: Rows of the SPEC risk table about deletion, groups, grading_type/points and late policy covered end to end against FakeCanvas with seeded submissions; after deleting every assignment locally and pushing, every seeded submission still exists unchanged (assert on FakeCanvas state); push then fetch is a no-op; tests pass.

title: Submission guard and pre-push backup

Assignment group deletion is always GuardBlocked (and not in the allowlist). Late policy comes from GET /courses/{c}/late_policy.
acceptance_criteria: Every row of the SPEC risk table has a test; hard blocks can't be bypassed by any confirmed flag; backup uses only GET (assert via fake.log) and aborts push on failure; tests pass.
notes: From PR #5 (FakeCanvas): use fake.seed_submissions / snapshot_submissions / assert_submissions_intact(snap). The fake's assignments module must never touch fake.submissions on assignment delete; the guard tests should assert deletion of an assignment with submissions is refused before any DELETE reaches the fake (check fake.log).

title: fetch_course, `canvas clone` and `canvas fetch`, stability suite

title: CanvasClient with endpoint allowlist and rate limiting
description: Implement remote/http.py and remote/allowlist.py: pagination, 3-step file upload, download, rate-limit backoff, read/write modes, and allowlist enforcement before any I/O.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md 'Enforcement layers' (layer 1); CONTRACTS.md section 7.
Owns: remote/http.py, remote/allowlist.py, tests/test_allowlist.py, tests/test_http.py.
High risk: this is safety layer 1. tests/test_allowlist.py must include an explicit list of forbidden calls (any write under /submissions, DELETE course, DELETE discussion_topics, quizzes, enrollments writes, assignment_group DELETE without move_assignments_to) and assert each raises ForbiddenEndpoint without a request being sent. Use httpx.MockTransport in these tests (FakeCanvas comes in F5).
Course lock: the client is bound to one course_id and {c} in the allowlist matches only that id. Assignment group DELETE is not allowed at all (CONTRACTS section 7). GET /courses/{c}/late_policy is allowed (the guard needs it).
acceptance_criteria: Forbidden-call list all raise before I/O; read mode rejects every non-GET; pagination via Link headers returns all pages; 403 rate-limit and 5xx retried with backoff then CanvasAPIError; upload performs the 3 steps and returns file JSON; tests pass. A client for course A can't reach any /courses/B path; assignment group DELETE is forbidden.
close_reason: PR #3 merged. Allowlist exact METHOD+path, {c}=own course, ASCII regex; denied names only in resource positions (page slugs OK). Writes retried only on throttling (403 rate limit / 429), 5xx retried for GET/DELETE only: apply must not assume POST retries. PUT/DELETE /files/N and writes under /folders/N do 1-2 extra GETs to verify folder context is this course. _method override rejected. Upload step 2 https-only, never Canvas origin, no token.

title: Canonical serialization, model base and course loading
description: Implement model/serialize.py, model/base.py (Kind, ObjectKey, CanvasObject, TypeSpec, REGISTRY) and model/course.py (Course, load_tree, dump_tree) driven by the registry, so type beads plug in without editing course.py. Add a reusable fixed-point test helper that every type bead uses.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md 'Serialization: the part that has to be right'; CONTRACTS.md sections 2, 4, 5.
Owns: model/serialize.py, model/base.py, model/course.py, model/__init__.py (registry), tests/test_serialize.py, tests/helpers/fixed_point.py.
This is the foundation of merge quality: false diffs after a fetch mean false conflicts. Be strict about determinism (key order, quoting, trailing newline, list style).
model/__init__.py already registers all five TypeSpecs (scaffold stubs). Keep it that way: type beads must not need to edit model/__init__.py or course.py. TypeSpec must fit files (_meta.yaml + blobs) and modules (one modules.yaml) as well as one-file-per-object types.
Tolerant input: CRLF, BOM, missing trailing newline. Canonical output: LF, UTF-8, no BOM.
acceptance_criteria: dump is deterministic across runs and Python hash seeds (test with PYTHONHASHSEED variations); fixed-point helper asserts dump(load(dump(c))) == dump(c); tolerant load (date-only, shuffled keys) normalizes to canonical form; tests pass.
close_reason: PR #4 merged. TypeSpec load/dump documented in CONTRACTS §4. Type beads call tests/helpers/fixed_point.py (assert_spec_fixed_point/assert_spec_normalizes; files bead also assert_files_meta_fixed_point and implements optional FilesMetaSpec). Absent == null == no value (§5). dump_yaml nested_orders for nested key orders. python-frontmatter unused. dump_tree writes course.yaml/roster.yaml; duplicate module names keyed positionally (#name#2).

title: Scaffold the Python package, tooling and CI
description: uv project with the layout in CONTRACTS.md section 1: every module created as a stub with the documented signatures raising NotImplementedError; typer CLI `canvas` with all commands registered as stubs; pytest, ruff, pyright (strict on src/), hypothesis; GitHub Actions running the quality gate; pandoc installed in CI.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md sections 1 and 12.
Owns: pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .github/workflows/ci.yml, all stub files under src/canvas_sync/ and tests/ (later beads replace stub bodies), tests/conftest.py (registers the `integration` marker, skipped unless env vars set).
Keep stubs importable and type-correct so pyright passes from day one.
Also: create tests/fake_canvas/ as a package of stub modules (core, pages, discussion_topics, assignments, files, modules) and model/__init__.py registering all five TypeSpec stubs, so parallel beads never edit shared registration files.
pyright strict: ruamel.yaml, pypandoc and python-frontmatter have weak or missing stubs. Configure per-module overrides in pyproject.toml rather than sprinkling ignores; say which in the PR.
conftest.py: an `integration` fixture that builds a write client only when CANVAS_SANDBOX_COURSE is set and equals the course id under test (CONTRACTS section 7, course lock).
acceptance_criteria: `uv sync && uv run pytest && uv run ruff check && uv run ruff format --check && uv run pyright` passes locally and in CI; `uv run canvas --help` lists clone, fetch, pull, push, status, diff, validate, open.
close_reason: PR #1 merged. CanvasClient takes course_id (contract §7); FetchContext/ApplyContext in remote/context.py. ruff excludes *.md. ALLOWED list empty. CLI does not yet map CanvasSyncError to exit 1.

title: [human] Canvas API token and sandbox course
description: Get a personal access token for UBC Canvas (Account > Settings > New access token) and a sandbox/dev course where the tool may write freely. Enrol or enable a test student (Student View) so submissions can be seeded. Check whether UBC restricts tokens; if so, find out how to get a developer key.
design: Token goes in the CANVAS_TOKEN env var only, never in a file in the repo. Record sandbox URL and course id (not the token) with `bd remember`.
acceptance_criteria: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANVAS_TOKEN' https://canvas.ubc.ca/api/v1/users/self` succeeds; sandbox course id known; test student can submit.
notes: Token works. Sandbox = course 198014 (owner decision). Remaining: owner opens Student View once in the Canvas UI to create the test student (API shows 0 StudentViewEnrollment), then confirm a test submission works.

title: Preserve unsupported module items and module settings across fetch/push
description: The modules model (PR #11) supports 7 item types (page, assignment, file, header, url, quiz, discussion) and doesn't model prerequisites, require_sequential_progress or completion requirements. Real courses have external-tool items and these settings. If fetch drops them, the next push sees them as removed locally and deletes or alters them on Canvas. Data loss (not submissions), but silent.
design: Options: model unsupported items as opaque {unmanaged: {type, canvas_id, title}} entries kept in position and never written; carry module settings opaquely; or have the modules differ never emit DELETE for items/settings it cannot represent. Prerequisites must be keyed by canvas_id, not name. Touches model/modules.py, the modules reader (6fk.5) and the differ (orx.6).
acceptance_criteria: Fetch of a course with an external-tool item and a module with prerequisites/completion requirements, then push with no local change: zero operations. Editing another item in that module does not remove or alter the unsupported item or settings.

title: [human-assisted] Full round trip on the sandbox

acceptance_criteria: Every step passes or has a bug bead filed.

title: [human-assisted] File replacement experiment on the sandbox

design: Small script using CanvasClient in write mode against the sandbox only, kept under tests/integration/experiments/. Owner checks Student View. Record results in this bead's notes; P5 and FakeCanvas depend on them.
acceptance_criteria: Notes answer each question in the SPEC test plan.

Unless PR #3 adds a client-side ownership check, this writer must confirm the file/folder belongs to the course (folder context_type=Course, context_id=c) before any write.

title: FakeCanvas test transport (core)
description: tests/fake_canvas.py: an in-memory httpx transport that behaves like Canvas for the core endpoints: course, sections, users/enrollments, group categories and groups, pagination, Link headers, request log, seeded submissions on assignments (stored, never written by the tool), and a stable non-identity HTML sanitizer.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md section 12, section 7 (endpoint list).
Owns: tests/fake_canvas/core.py and __init__.py (the per-resource modules stay stubs for reader/writer beads to fill); tests/fixtures/canvas/*.json shapes taken from Canvas API docs; tests/test_fake_canvas.py.
Invented people only in fixtures.
Unknown or non-allowlisted write requests make the fake fail the test (CONTRACTS section 12).
acceptance_criteria: CanvasClient (F4) works against FakeCanvas for course/sections/users/groups; pagination works with small page sizes; fake.log records method, path, params; tests pass.
close_reason: PR #5 merged. Plug in via fake.route(method, regex, handler) in tests/fake_canvas/<resource>.py register(fake); regexes match the decoded path relative to /api/v1, {c}=course id; module routes override core. Non-GET without route or refused by allowlist raises FakeCanvasError; non-API writes need upload_target=True. seed_submissions/snapshot_submissions/assert_submissions_intact deep-copy. fake.fail()/fake.throttle() inject faults. sanitize_html idempotent. fake.client(mode) gives a real CanvasClient.

title: git plumbing, snapshots, blob store and .canvasignore
description: Implement gitops.py, snapshot.py (snapshot(), BlobStore) and ignore.py exactly as in CONTRACTS.md section 11. snapshot builds trees with git plumbing without touching the working tree and updates refs/remotes/canvas/main with compare-and-swap.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md 'Core idea: Canvas is a git remote', 'Push rules'; CONTRACTS.md section 11.
Owns: gitops.py, snapshot.py, ignore.py and tests (use tmp git repos).
High risk: a wrong update_ref or a working-tree write here can lose user work. Never run porcelain commands that modify the work tree except in merge()/commit_paths().
snapshot() also writes .canvas/bodies.json (Bodies.dump) into the tree and takes extra_parent: push passes HEAD so canvas/main descends from the pushed commit. Provide fast_forward() (git merge --ff-only) instead of a write-back commit helper. See CONTRACTS section 11.
acceptance_criteria: snapshot of an unchanged Course returns None and creates no commit; nested trees and binary blobs written correctly; update_ref fails if the ref moved; is_ancestor, unmerged_paths, conflict_marker_paths, is_clean correct in tmp repos with real merge conflicts; ignore globs behave like gitignore; tests pass. snapshot with extra_parent creates a two-parent commit even when the tree is unchanged; fast_forward refuses when not possible.
notes: From PR #4 review: model dump_tree writes course.yaml with non-default fields only and drops comments. Fetch/snapshot must not overwrite the user's course.yaml with that output unless the parsed config actually differs.
close_reason: PR #10 merged. snapshot() via temp GIT_INDEX_FILE, CAS update_ref (RefMoved only on CAS mismatch, GitError otherwise). course.yaml bytes carried from previous canvas/main when parsed config equal (HEAD only on first snapshot). gitops.read_file_at, tree_of, BlobStore.has. merge uses --allow-unrelated-histories (fetch must check course id, see 6fk.6 note); merge fails on unborn HEAD so first pull uses fast_forward. Bodies still a stub (ixy.2). No roster.yaml carry-over.

title: Config, dates and error types
description: Implement config.py (CourseConfig, load_config, get_token), dates.py (parse_local, format_local, to_canvas, from_canvas, default-time rules) and errors.py.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md 'course.yaml', 'Dates and visibility'; CONTRACTS.md sections 3 and 9 (errors).
Owns: src/canvas_sync/config.py, dates.py, errors.py and their tests.
DST: test a Vancouver date on both sides of the March and November transitions; ambiguous/nonexistent local times resolve with fold=0 and that choice is documented in the docstring.
acceptance_criteria: Round trip from_canvas(to_canvas(x)) == x for local times across DST; date-only inputs pick the right default time per key; invalid timezone or missing token raises ConfigError with a one-line message; tests pass.
close_reason: PR #2 merged. format_local writes HH:MM, or HH:MM:SS when seconds are nonzero (keeps Canvas 23:59:59). Fall-back fold=1 hour re-parses as fold=0: documented in CONTRACTS §3; use is_ambiguous_local to warn. Compare dates via to_canvas strings or local values. CourseConfig has extra=forbid; tz exact-match; parse_local rejects non-str.
